title: When Four Classes Refuse to Be Equal

scenes.tts: Why do two test-cross classes overwhelm the other two? A blue chromosome and a gold partner pair in meiosis. Each carries the same marker positions. Their allele combinations begin intact, yet the offspring bins grow unevenly. The puzzle is what those bins reveal about gametes.
scenes.caption: Why do two test-cross classes overwhelm the other two? A blue chromosome and a gold partner pair in meiosis. Each carries the same marker positions. Their allele combinations begin intact, yet the offspring bins grow unevenly. The puzzle is what those bins reveal about gametes.
scenes.visual: Hook picture fills the frame. Carry a thick BLUE chromosome labelled A—B above a thick GOLD chromosome labelled a—b. Four large offspring bins sit below; two rise high and two remain low. Keep every height marked 'schematic'. Slowly stream allele-pair tiles from the chromosome pair into the bins.
scenes.narration: Why do two test-cross classes overwhelm the other two? A blue chromosome and a gold partner pair in meiosis. Each carries the same marker positions. Their allele combinations begin intact, yet the offspring bins grow unevenly. The puzzle is what those bins reveal about gametes.

scenes.visual: Brief title over the same moving board: 'When Four Classes Refuse to Be Equal'. Chromosome tiles continue drifting gently behind the title.

scenes.tts: With scorable traits, a test cross makes one parent's gametes visible. The heterozygote can contribute big A big B or big A little b. It can also contribute little a big B or little a little b. The tester always contributes recessive alleles. Each offspring therefore carries a readable copy of the heterozygote's gamete.
scenes.caption: With scorable traits, a test cross makes one parent's gametes visible. The heterozygote can contribute A B or A b. It can also contribute a B or a b. The tester always contributes recessive alleles. Each offspring therefore carries a readable copy of the heterozygote's gamete.
scenes.visual: Transform the four bins into four large gamete tiles. A pale tester strip labelled a—b slides under each tile without changing. Each joined pair drops into the matching offspring bin, so the board visibly reads the heterozygote's gametes.
scenes.narration: With scorable traits, a test cross makes one parent's gametes visible. The heterozygote can contribute A B or A b. It can also contribute a B or a b. The tester always contributes recessive alleles. Each offspring therefore carries a readable copy of the heterozygote's gamete.

scenes.tts: Independent assortment would feed every bin equally. Instead, the inherited combinations repeatedly fill two bins faster. That excess is the signature of linkage in this cross. Linked means the loci share a chromosome closely enough for their association to appear in the scored progeny.
scenes.caption: Independent assortment would feed every bin equally. Instead, the inherited combinations repeatedly fill two bins faster. That excess is the signature of linkage in this cross. Linked means the loci share a chromosome closely enough for their association to appear in the scored progeny.
scenes.visual: Reset all four schematic bins to equal outlines labelled 'independent expectation'. Then stream BLUE A—B and GOLD a—b tiles faster so their bins rise above the two mixed bins. Bracket the excess pair with the label 'linkage pattern'.
scenes.narration: Independent assortment would feed every bin equally. Instead, the inherited combinations repeatedly fill two bins faster. That excess is the signature of linkage in this cross. Linked means the loci share a chromosome closely enough for their association to appear in the scored progeny.

scenes.tts: First read the chromosomes the heterozygote received. Big A with big B is one inherited combination. Little a with little b is the other. Those are parental, even before counting offspring. The mixed combinations are recombinant. This inherited arrangement is phase. Class size can support that assignment, but phase defines it.
scenes.caption: First read the chromosomes the heterozygote received. A B is one inherited combination. a b is the other. Those are parental, even before counting offspring. The mixed combinations are recombinant. This inherited arrangement is phase. Class size can support that assignment, but phase defines it.
scenes.visual: Highlight BLUE A—B and GOLD a—b with a bracket labelled 'inherited = parental'. Copy them into the two tall bins. Build the mixed A—b and a—B tiles from half BLUE and half GOLD, then place them in the shorter bins. Keep heights schematic.
scenes.narration: First read the chromosomes the heterozygote received. A B is one inherited combination. a b is the other. Those are parental, even before counting offspring. The mixed combinations are recombinant. This inherited arrangement is phase. Class size can support that assignment, but phase defines it.

scenes.tts: Each homologue has already copied itself, so four chromatids lie side by side. A crossover joins matching positions on non-sister chromatids. When the exchange falls between the markers, the right-hand segments trade places. Two chromatids keep their inherited combinations. The exchanged chromatids carry new combinations, which feed the recombinant bins.
scenes.caption: Each homologue has already copied itself, so four chromatids lie side by side. A crossover joins matching positions on non-sister chromatids. When the exchange falls between the markers, the right-hand segments trade places. Two chromatids keep their inherited combinations. The exchanged chromatids carry new combinations, which feed the recombinant bins.
scenes.visual: Reveal the carried pair as four thick chromatids already present, two per homologue; do not animate any copying step. Cross one BLUE and one GOLD chromatid between the marker dots. Animate a clean reciprocal segment swap. Preserve two unchanged chromatids. Slide all four products into their corresponding bins while origin colours remain visible.
scenes.narration: Each homologue has already copied itself, so four chromatids lie side by side. A crossover joins matching positions on non-sister chromatids. When the exchange falls between the markers, the right-hand segments trade places. Two chromatids keep their inherited combinations. The exchanged chromatids carry new combinations, which feed the recombinant bins.

scenes.tts: Now slide the right marker farther away while crossover positions keep appearing along the chromatids. Which pair of bins should claim a larger share over a short interval? Hold the chromosome picture in your mind.
scenes.caption: Now slide the right marker farther away while crossover positions keep appearing along the chromatids. Which pair of bins should claim a larger share over a short interval? Hold the chromosome picture in your mind.
scenes.visual: Move marker B slowly rightward on all chromatids. Small crossover sparks appear at evenly sampled schematic positions. Put a question mark over the two recombinant bins. Do not reveal a direction yet.
scenes.narration: Now slide the right marker farther away while crossover positions keep appearing along the chromatids. Which pair of bins should claim a larger share over a short interval? Hold the chromosome picture in your mind.

scenes.visual: Keep the widened marker interval, moving crossover sparks, and question mark. Let a thin scanning line sweep across the interval during the deliberate thinking pause.

scenes.tts: The recombinant pair grows. A wider interval offers more places for a crossover to land between the markers. Over a short interval, a second crossover between the markers is rare, so few exchanges stay hidden. The recombinant share can therefore serve as an estimate of genetic map distance.

scenes.visual: Remove the question mark. Stream more mixed-colour tiles into the recombinant bins as marker B moves right. Add the label 'schematic'. Then transform the paired recombinant bins into the numerator of RF = recombinants / total on screen.
scenes.narration: The recombinant pair grows. A wider interval offers more places for a crossover to land between the markers. Over a short interval, a second crossover between the markers is rare, so few exchanges stay hidden. The recombinant share can therefore serve as an estimate of genetic map distance.

scenes.tts: Add both recombinant classes before dividing by all offspring. Write the result as a percentage. For a short interval, that percentage estimates centimorgans on the genetic map. It does not measure a fixed length of DNA. Different chromosome regions and different sexes can convert physical spacing differently.

scenes.visual: Keep the formula large. Merge both recombinant bins into its numerator, then all bins into its denominator. Transform the percentage symbol into tick marks on a short chromosome ruler labelled 'genetic map'. Place a separate DNA-length bar below with a crossed-out equals sign.
scenes.narration: Add both recombinant classes before dividing by all offspring. Write the result as a percentage. For a short interval, that percentage estimates centimorgans on the genetic map. scenes.tts: The workflow is now stable. Read the parents. Name the parental and recombinant classes from phase. Add the recombinant classes, then divide by the total. Only then use the short-interval ruler. The next question is what happens when crossovers can hide one another.

scenes.visual: Animate four compact steps around the carried board: chromosomes to class labels to merged recombinant bin to short map ruler. Keep all objects moving gently. Fade everything except the short ruler before the end card.
scenes.narration: The workflow is now stable. Read the parents. Name the parental and recombinant classes from phase. Add the recombinant classes, then divide by the total. Only then use the short-interval ruler. The next question is what happens when crossovers can hide one another.

scenes.visual: Show one centered line only: 'For short intervals, recombination frequency estimates map distance.'
